comments.body:
PHASE 1 RCA — Ubuntu runner occupancy (2026-08-13)

Baseline and attribution
- GitHub Actions run 31752047186: workflow wall 27m46s. macOS default remains the completion critical path at 22m15s. Ubuntu default cells were py3.11=615s, py3.12=634s, py3.13=563s: 1,812 runner-seconds (30.2 runner-minutes) per Verified run. Ubuntu integration cells were 81/92/81s and complexity-lock invocations were 52/54/55s. Other >30s Ubuntu operations: optional-extras isolate 91s and tickets-history mount 39s. No individual integration test exceeded 30s.
- Individual >30s Ubuntu tests/fixtures: bridge cadence 130.59/110.97/100.66s and AST provenance fixture setup 46.95/49.02/48.84s.

Confirmed mechanisms and discriminating experiments
1. Bridge cadence — tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py:164-184 calls _bridge_schedule() inside the 1,440-minute comprehension, so the same workflow YAML is read and parsed 1,440 times. Local median current=7.925s; read+parse=7.653s; parse preloaded text=7.584s; reuse one parsed schedule=0.00106s; cached schedule while retaining all 1,440 checks=0.000383s. This kills the hypothesis that exhaustive minute arithmetic is expensive: YAML parsing is the cost. Introduced by 432a92c165; prior 2b136e74e7 loaded once. Estimated Ubuntu saving from the measured CI cells is 342.22s / 5.70 runner-minutes per Verified run. Defect legitimacy: the existing test contract requires exhaustive uniform-cadence proof, not repeated I/O; hoisting restores the earlier invariant-loading pattern without changing any checked minute.
2. render_unit existential assertion — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py:308-325 calls real Pandoc for all 232 eligible prose units, but asserts only eligible>0 and changed>0. Current=7.887s and 232 subprocesses. Exact short-circuit evaluation reaches both witnesses in 0.035s with 1 subprocess. Forced identity-renderer and no-eligible mutations fail identically under both forms, so this preserves the assertion and is not minute/content sampling.
3. Pandoc hardening oracle — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py:65-98 and :440-458 executes both current _convert and a copied _legacy_convert for all 884 units. Combined corpus+hardening under -n4 invoked Pandoc 3,421 times (workers 890/652/974/905); wall 45.60s, user 45.02s, sys 50.77s. Corpus alone=29.52s; hardening alone=18.80s. Serial conversion median=33ms, p95=35.6ms, max=70.6ms, so aggregate process startup dominates. Cross-worker pass-1 sharing is working; duplicate cache fill is not the cause. Mutating shared _PANDOC_TO to plain kept current and copied legacy in agreement for all 884 units, proving the live-vs-live oracle is coupled. A static immutable expected baseline detected 799/884 such mutations while continuing to run product _convert through real Pandoc for every unit. Safe immediate repair: replace only the duplicated legacy subprocess side with immutable expected outputs; keep all 884 live product conversions. Full per-change substitution of real Pandoc conflicts with accepted ADR 0095 (every conversion assertion uses the real binary), so that broader option remains in architecture RESEARCH and requires explicit acknowledgment/supersession before drafting or implementation.
4. AST provenance setup — the three Ubuntu cells spend 46.95/49.02/48.84s in setup. Parsing is already cached by closed analogical-dashing-fennecfox. Focused local setup=3.37s; cProfile records ~9.54M ast.walk iterations and ~130.9M calls. The fixture repeatedly rediscovers enclosing callers and parent relationships. Build caller/parent indices once per process while preserving the exact 24 (key, expr, verdict) tuples and all existing guards.
5. Complexity lock — .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:449-455 runs the same OS/Python-invariant static policy in every matrix cell (Ubuntu 52/54/55s; macOS 45s). Move one invocation into the existing lint job and delete four duplicates. Estimated net saving ~154 runner-seconds / 2.57 runner-minutes per Verified run; coverage is unchanged because the policy is evaluated once on the same commit.
6. Jira DC — Verified uses -m "not integration and not external". tests/external/live_jira_dc collects zero tests in Verified (62 deselected); the weekly/manual external harness runs 63 tests and takes 2,384–2,635s. It is already outside the hot path, so moving it saves exactly 0 seconds. Jira/DC-oriented hermetic unit files provide the smaller substitute already: 472 passed in 6.67s under -n4, slowest 0.76s. Removing them would save only seconds and reduce coverage.
7. Mutation testing — from closed cryptic-damp-panda: 62 successful post-addition runs, only 5 selected mutation shards, and mutation was never the last prerequisite, so measured completion-path addition=0. Selector-only cost ~0.42 runner-min/run. Selected mutation averages ~50.1 runner-min and can contribute contention, but it does not explain the observed completion-latency regression.

OSS consensus and tracker checks
- Hoist/share invariants: pytest uses session-scoped invariant fixtures; Django uses setUpTestData; Pylint/Astroid precedent is recorded on analogical-dashing-fennecfox.
- Existential short-circuit: pytest testing/test_nodes.py, Django tests/asgi/tests.py, and CPython importlib metadata tests use any(...).
- Static/golden oracle paired with live implementation: Pandoc test/Tests/Writers/Jira.hs uses literal expected writer output; Kubernetes client-go/dynamic/golden_test.go uses committed fixtures; Rust compiletest uses blessed .stderr/.stdout fixtures.
- Small real boundary plus fast substitutes: nbconvert and pypandoc use small real Pandoc contracts; OpenTofu mock_provider, Kubernetes fake clientsets/httptest, and pycontribs/jira requests_mock keep routine checks hermetic.
- Static policy once outside language matrices: CPython lint.yml, Django linters.yml, and Rust/Kubernetes tidy/verify surfaces.
All surveyed projects were active on 2026-08-12/13; popularity: Pandoc 45.8k, Rust 115k, Kubernetes 124k, pytest 14.4k, Django 88.4k, CPython 74.3k, OpenTofu 29.8k, nbconvert 1.9k, pypandoc 1.1k, pycontribs/jira 2.1k stars. Each immediate remediation clears the ticket-defined >=2/3 consensus rule.
- Prior tickets searched: cryptic-damp-panda (original RCA), harmless-wavy-osprey (xdist sharing), albinic-agrologic-dolphin and ashy-waterlog-hamadryas (Pandoc hardening), analogical-dashing-fennecfox (first AST cache), humble-cinnamoned-mussel (complexity merge-base correctness), coercive-paediatric-bug (rejects extra sharding/workers without aggregate savings), dimmed-supersweet-xenarthra (deferred production Pandoc spawn-cost idea). No rejection found for schedule hoisting, exact existential short-circuiting, immutable legacy oracle, AST indexing, or one-time complexity invocation.

Phase-1 conclusion
The proven Ubuntu levers are redundant work, not reduced coverage or added parallelism. Proceed on separate linked implementation tickets for the five consensus-backed repairs. Jira routing needs no change. Full static substitution for all Pandoc conversion assertions is held at architecture RESEARCH because it would supersede ADR 0095.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ARCHITECTURE RESEARCH — bounded live Pandoc boundary plus static corpus (2026-08-14; no ADR draft or implementation yet).

Current constraint: accepted ADR 0095 states that every conversion assertion uses real pinned Pandoc and no test monkeypatches it. The shipped dependency is pypandoc-binary==1.15 / Pandoc 3.6.1. The committed legacy fixture pins darwin-arm64 SHA-256 94ebf1efbce3561379e8f25de3efe5aeabee64dc36dd8e8b9e96cf05b4195c52 and linux-x86_64 4715627586c5d9c732e8f5a6b6bb9e27c4216a76a7729e043b24374dedf8a1f0. Therefore full hot-path substitution requires an explicit ADR 0095 supersession; it cannot be treated as an implementation detail.

Current cost and boundary map: a fresh same-host macOS three-worker run of test_wiki_render_corpus.py plus test_wiki_render_hardening.py passed 51 tests in 38.64s / real 38.80s (user 27.56s, sys 25.32s). Run 31798375024 attributed 149.03s setup to the shared pass-1 corpus and 35.29s to the prose fixed-point call; those two visible phases alone are a 184.32s critical-path lower bound, excluding the hardening chunks that each stay below 30s. The corpus tests assert cardinality/secrets, protected excerpts, exact tables/comments, deterministic settling, richness ratios, and a non-vacuous live dispatch. The hardening suite asserts all 884 prepared inputs and immutable expected outputs align, exact binary provenance, and product _convert bytes equal the landed golden bytes for every input. A superseding design must preserve these assertion classes by running segmentation/preservation/fixed-point logic against committed pre-rendered pass outputs in Verify, retain a small representative real _convert/Pandoc contract on both gating platforms, and move the complete real-Pandoc replay of every corpus unit and every settling pass to the existing weekly/manual external-integration workflow. Pin drift must fail fast and the existing deterministic generator remains the regeneration path.

Verified upstream practice (source read at pinned current branch SHAs):
- Pandoc 03a0a6484321: test/Tests/Writers/Jira.hs uses literal expected Jira writer outputs for compact construct cases.
- nbconvert 78ed30837a60: tests/filters/test_pandoc.py and tests/utils/test_pandoc.py use only small real Pandoc probes (relative-path pair and empty/version/availability calls), not a repeated production-sized corpus.
- pypandoc f57e9ab51049: tests/test_pypandoc.py uses small representative real conversions and explicitly says broader format coverage would test Pandoc rather than pypandoc.
- Kubernetes client-go 3fcdd4c72588: dynamic/golden_test.go stores committed request/response fixtures and drives the client through httptest/fake transports rather than a real cluster; UPDATE_DYNAMIC_CLIENT_FIXTURES is the explicit regeneration switch.
- Rust 059bf4a660dd: rustc-dev-guide UI tests store blessed .stdout/.stderr snapshots, require compact in-source diagnostic annotations as an independent anti-mistake oracle, and normalize platform noise.
All five repositories are active and unarchived; current stars were Pandoc 45,865, nbconvert 1,933, pypandoc 1,151, client-go 9,865, and Rust 115,504. No surveyed source documents rejecting bounded live probes plus static/golden routine assertions for reliability. The ticket-defined >=2/3 consensus threshold passes.

Research critique before DRAFT: (1) unverified assumption: exact post-refactor Verify cost remains an estimate until a RED/GREEN implementation run; current lower bound is 184.32s macOS CI and same-host removable wall is 38.80s. (2) dependency still to investigate during DRAFT: none for the architectural boundary; GitHub schedule and current generator/provenance route are already inspected. (3) unanswered: exact representative input set must be chosen by strata and mutation sensitivity during TDD, not in the ADR. (4) conflict: ADR 0095 is direct and must be marked Superseded by the new record in the same change. Per the architecture-decision lifecycle, DRAFT is gated on explicit team confirmation of this research summary.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ARCHITECTURE RESEARCH CONFIRMATION + CRITIQUE (2026-08-14). Operator explicitly confirmed the research findings and authorized continuation to the ADR lifecycle. Numbered pre-DRAFT critique required by architecture-decisions:

1. Assumptions not verified: the 184.32s saving is a one-run CI lower bound, not yet a paired A/B result. This does not block the architecture choice, but the implementation ticket must measure before/after on the same host and the first genuine Verify run; do not promise exactly 184.32s. Cross-platform output identity is already verified by the current single immutable output fixture running against platform-specific pinned binaries and hashes on Linux x86_64 and Darwin arm64.
2. Dependencies not investigated: none remain among Pandoc 3.6.1, pypandoc-binary 1.15, current corpus/generator, pytest/xdist, GitHub Actions routing, and the surveyed upstream projects. The current external-integration workflow was inspected and is weekly/manual but all existing jobs are ubuntu-latest; it has no macOS arm today.
3. Questions the research did not answer: (a) exact representative live-Pandoc sample; recommendation is one deterministic contract body per corpus stratum (code_arrow/table/prose), selected to exercise real conversion, protected fallback, and fixed-point handling, plus the existing compact pin/provenance construct probes; (b) platform cadence for full replay; recommendation is a dedicated weekly/manual Pandoc job matrix on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, so moving full corpus replay does not reduce the currently gated platform boundary.
4. Conflicts with existing decisions: ADR 0095 states every conversion assertion uses the real binary. The new ADR must narrowly supersede that testing-assurance sentence while preserving the production segmenting renderer, Pandoc pin, Linux/macOS provenance, safety/fallback invariants, and every assertion class. The repository uses docs/adr plus numbered/index gates rather than the generic docs/decisions layout; project AGENTS.md governs that location.

Pre-DRAFT recommendations requiring explicit operator disposition: accept the three-body representative live contract plus existing compact probes, accept a weekly/manual Linux+macOS full replay, and accept paired post-implementation measurement rather than treating 184.32s as guaranteed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PHASE 1 RCA — same-change Verify cancellation regression (2026-08-14)

Problem
A replacement Gerrit Verify run for the same change can remain pending while the superseded run continues consuming runners. Run 31834896849 waited 25m10s before its first job and finished in 57m29s.

Proven root cause
Commit 6f4123678c (docs-only routing) added job-level always() predicates to every full-route reusable job in .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml (current lines 222, 234, 251, 267, 281, 295, and 350). On a superseding patchset, the predecessor prerequisites remain successful and route=full, so those predicates re-evaluate true. GitHub therefore does not send cancellation to the stale jobs. The stale run keeps the same-change concurrency slot until its test matrix finishes naturally, so the replacement has no job to queue.

Discriminating proof
- Across 12 same-change overlaps in the latest 100 completed runs, successor first-job creation occurred within 0–1s of predecessor termination. The initial hold is concurrency admission, not runner acquisition.
- In the post-6f412 outlier, predecessor 31834162663 kept four pytest jobs alive after successor creation. They ended as ordinary held-out assertion failures at +14s, +49s, +214s, and +1,499s; none concluded cancelled. The predecessor consumed 1,785 runner-seconds after the replacement existed.
- The macOS log reports 1 failed, 13,173 passed in 1,852.36s and no cancellation message. The successor clear job was created only after the predecessor vote completed.
- Pre-6f412 controls with the same pytest/xdist command show explicit The operation was canceled messages and cancelled conclusions within 25–104s.
- Runner scarcity is rejected for this hold: the successor clear job started 3s after it was finally created.
- A bad concurrency key is rejected: all overlap pairs were the same Gerrit change, and admission unlocked exactly when the predecessor terminated.
- Pytest signal handling is rejected: pre-6f412 xdist jobs terminate when the cancellation request is actually sent.

Authority and OSS consensus
GitHub docs commit 81ade08c, workflow-cancellation.md lines 18–22, explicitly states that running jobs whose if condition remains true are not canceled and names if: always() as the example. The original smoky-flare-slug contract requires new patchsets to auto-cancel prior runs. The docs-only ticket brainy-accused-wrasse requires full fallback on classifier failure, but cancellation is not classifier failure. Home Assistant, Apache Airflow, and Grafana all combine cancellation concurrency with cancellation-aware !cancelled() fan-in/report predicates.

Legitimate remediation
Replace the full-route job-level always() status check with a cancellation-aware status check while retaining the existing prerequisite and route expression. This preserves full fallback on classifier failure, preserves every successful-patchset job and assertion, and removes only obsolete-patchset work. No prior ticket rejection was found; frowsy-beggarly-mammoth concerns triage wording, not cancellation behavior.

comments.body:
OUTLIER RCA — the 57m29s and 50m29s failures (2026-08-14)

Run 31834896849 (57m29s, failure): the first job did not start until 1,513s (25m13s) after workflow creation. The macOS matrix cell began 1,609s after creation and then occupied 1,823s (30m23s). Its default pytest step was 1,697s / 28m17s and failed at the end on test_completion_fail_renders_failure_findings_fallback. Individual >30s phases were old pre-ADR-0096 Pandoc corpus fixture setup 142.11s, editor loopback setup 35.18s, and old real-Pandoc prose fixed-point call 34.06s. Ubuntu cells failed the same test after default steps of 413/442/629s; optional-extras install was 100s; tickets history mount was 44s. Total runner occupancy was 4,097s despite the 3,449s wall because initial org runner starvation dominated.

Run 31841305299 (50m29s, failure): the first job waited 1,453s (24m13s); macOS began 1,535s after creation and ran 1,479s (24m39s). macOS default/integration steps were 1,272s and 121s. The old Pandoc corpus setup was 143.48s and editor setup 35.05s; no Ubuntu individual test exceeded 30s. Mutation ran five long shards (814/705/483/455/337s) and total runner occupancy was 6,914s (115.23 runner-minutes). The run failed a separate lint/complexity gate, but fail-fast:false deliberately allowed the full diagnostic matrix to finish.

Interpretation: the >50m examples are additive, not a single 57m test path: ~24–25m org-wide runner starvation before admission plus ~25–30m macOS execution. The full real-Pandoc corpus phases in these old runs have since moved to External Integration Tests (18f58da624), removing the 142–143s fixture and full replay calls from current Verify. The remaining recurrent >30s individual phase is editor loopback setup, now instrumented by change 1793.

Rejected lever confirmed from tracker history: ad63-17ad-d545-45d4 explicitly preserved fail-fast:false diagnostics when collapsing optionality fan-out. Cancelling sibling cells on the first failure would reduce failed-run occupancy but would reduce failure/coverage diagnostics, contrary to this session constraint and prior decision, so it is not proposed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION / DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE for the outlier queue attribution

The 24–25 minute pre-start waits in the two >50m failures were NOT generic org runner starvation. They were same-change workflow-concurrency blocking under the pre-1792 cancellation bug:
- 31834162663 and 31834896849 were both Gerrit change 1788. The predecessor ended cancelled at 20:13:07; the 57m successor first started at 20:13:09 after waiting 1,513s.
- 31840710117 and 31841305299 were both change 1790. The predecessor ended cancelled at 21:35:17; the 50m successor first started at 21:35:18 after waiting 1,453s.
- Unrelated changes ran concurrently during both intervals, excluding a project-wide serialization explanation.

Thus the 57m/50m tail is already addressed by merged change 1792 (4cbaa19315, cancel superseded Verify jobs), subject to its still-open organic replacement proof on esthetic-degrading-pupa. Generic runner contention remains real for aggregate capacity, but it is not the causal attribution of these two initial waits. The current post-fix remaining problem is the ordinary no-queue macOS execution tail, which sampled 29m38s–34m21s end to end in runs 31837971444/31842940708/31843821793.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
The completed Gerrit Verified latency RCA optimized the macOS completion path, but Ubuntu jobs still occupy scarce org-wide runners for 11-14 minutes and contribute to queue contention. Follow-up questions identify three candidate levers: replace repeated Pandoc corpus rendering with static expected results plus a smaller boundary test, remove redundant work from the exhaustive 1,440-minute bridge cadence proof, and determine whether expensive Jira DC-oriented default-tier tests can move out of the per-change hot path while retaining fast unit coverage. The genuinely live tests/external/live_jira_dc suite is already excluded from Gerrit Verified by the `not external` selector and runs in its dedicated harness; moving that suite again would save zero. This work must preserve behavioral coverage and must not use extra parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner usage.

## Plan
- Build a dated Ubuntu runner-time dossier from final post-remediation run 31752047186, pytest duration logs, workflow routing, and focused local runtime experiments.
- For Pandoc and render_unit, map every current assertion to the code boundary it exercises. Include both full-corpus consumers: test_wiki_render_corpus.py (~884 pass-1 subprocesses plus additional passes) and test_wiki_render_hardening.py (~1,768 subprocesses for byte-equivalence). Compare static golden fixtures, a bounded real-Pandoc contract sample, and full-corpus external execution using defect-seeded experiments to detect any coverage loss. Treat the pinned Pandoc-version-to-output coupling as an explicit external boundary. Any accepted golden fixture must identify its Pandoc version and binary fingerprint, provide a documented regeneration command, and include a fast drift assertion that fails when the installed Pandoc version differs. The full real-Pandoc corpus must remain in the scheduled external-integration workflow as the revalidation destination, including after pin changes.
- For the bridge cadence test, discriminate between the cost of the 1,440 arithmetic checks and invariant workflow YAML I/O; prefer hoisting invariant I/O if it preserves the exhaustive proof.
